summary: Three newly added, reviewed Reuters stories cover China-US trade discussions, Tesla customer invitations and China's diabetes-drug reimbursement. This is a partial catch-up update, not a complete scan.
limitations: Targeted Reuters coverage only. The most recent fully completed scan remains unverified, and this update does not fill the historical publication backlog.

Only publication dates are verified for these sources. Exact original publication and development times are unknown; inclusion does not establish that events occurred inside this report window. Stories are conservatively labelled catch-up.
Two source follow-ups, on Bank of England policy and US air-traffic disruption, are held because their earlier versions are absent from the retained public history.
No market-price reaction attributable to these reports was independently established.

sources.title: China and US hold first trade-council discussions
Tesla invites selected customers to buy Cybercab
China adds Pfizer and Innovent diabetes drugs to reimbursement

stories.headline: China and US hold first trade-council discussions
stories.body: China's commerce ministry said the countries held their first trade-council meeting by video on Friday. The discussion covered tariffs, agricultural trade and earlier economic commitments. The report did not announce a completed agreement.
stories.analysis: A new negotiating forum could affect trade-sensitive businesses. Discussions alone do not establish tariff relief or new purchases.
stories.watch_next: Published terms and subsequent official statements.

stories.headline: Tesla invites selected customers to buy Cybercab
stories.body: Reuters reported that Tesla said on Friday it was inviting selected customers to buy Cybercab for personal use.
stories.analysis: Invitations may open a further route to customers, but they do not establish completed deliveries or recognised revenue.
stories.watch_next: Confirmed deliveries and the final terms offered to customers.

stories.headline: China adds Pfizer and Innovent diabetes drugs to reimbursement
stories.body: Reuters reported that Pfizer's ecnoglutide and Innovent's mazdutide will join China's state health-insurance scheme for type 2 diabetes from January 1.
stories.analysis: Reimbursement could broaden access and treatment volumes; the commercial effect also depends on pricing and uptake.
stories.watch_next: Reimbursement terms, patient uptake and company sales disclosures.
